A semi-literal English rendering of Liebermann’s German, created for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic. It is a crib to help the reader with Liebermann’s German, and should not be treated as a separate translation

A relatively literal English rendering of the Latin text of the Instituta Cnuti, created for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic. It is a crib to help the reader with the Latin, and should not be treated as a separate translation. Liebermann’s kinds of type (bold, spaced, smaller type, round brackets) are carried over onto the English words that render the marked Latin

witness.note: Instituta Cnuti (Latin translation of Anglo-Saxon laws, c. 1100): Liebermann’s edited text, from the manuscripts listed below
Strood, Medway Archive and Local Studies Centre, MS DRc/R1 (Textus Roffensis; formerly Rochester, Cathedral Library, MS A.3.5)
Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Rawlinson C 641
London, British Library, Cotton MS Titus A.xxvii
Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Lat. 4771, formerly Colbert 3860
London, Lambeth Palace Library, MS 118 (formerly of Merton priory, then Lord Lumley’s)
Phillipps MS 8078 (in 1903 owned by H. S. Nichols & Co., London)
